draft.title: Invasion, colonisation or settlement
card: Settlement
a word often used by British colonists and in older histories. It stresses people arriving and setting up homes, farms and towns.
Colonisation
a word for one country taking control of another place and ruling it as a colony. It describes what Britain did, without saying whether it was right or wrong.
Invasion
a word for entering a place by force to take it over. Many Aboriginal people use it, because the land was already owned and cared for by their peoples and was taken without agreement.
The words differ because people see 1788 from different perspectives. A historian can ask who is speaking and what each word leaves out.
draft.remember: Each word for 1788 shows a perspective. Many Aboriginal people see it as an invasion.

a.q: Why do some people say invasion and others say settlement when describing 1788?
opts: They view the same events from different perspectives
They are describing two different years in history
Only one of the words is ever used by historians
Aboriginal people arrived in Australia after 1788
a.why: The words come from different points of view about the same events. The option about two different years is tempting but wrong, because all the words describe 1788.
a.clue: Think about who is telling the story.

b.q: Mia reads a textbook that says Britain 'settled' Australia. Her friend Jai, who is Aboriginal, says it was an invasion. What is the best way for Mia to understand their different words?
opts: Ask who each speaker is and what their word leaves out
Decide that the older word must be the correct one
Assume that Jai is wrong because the book is printed
Avoid all three words because none of them can be used
b.why: Each word reflects a perspective, so asking who is speaking and what the word leaves out helps Mia judge it. Picking the older word or the printed book is tempting, but age or print does not make a perspective the only one.
b.clue: A good historian asks who is speaking.

a.best: They view the same events from different perspectives

b.best: Ask who each speaker is and what their word leaves out

problems.detail: The clue 'A good historian asks who is speaking' nearly restates the right option. It is the only option that mentions who is speaking, so a student can match the words without understanding perspective.

check.summary: The card and both answers are accurate and match the explanations. The only issue is that question b's clue echoes the right option almost word for word, which gives the answer away.
